# Anti-tells: what makes text read as machine-written

Scan every draft for these before calling it done. Each one is a reason to revise.

- A closing paragraph that explains the scene.
- Rhetorical tricolons ("It was X. It was Y. It was Z.").
- "A testament to", "a reminder that", "in that moment", "little did he know".
- Em-dashes, especially as a substitute for a comma or a period.
- Curly quotes.
- Every character described as "haunted", "ruthless", "rebellious", "visionary".
- Stock names: Blackwood, Thorne, Vance, Seraphina, Elias (as a default).
- Themes listed as abstract nouns and then dramatized one by one.
- Weather that matches the mood on cue.
- A "secret" that is announced as a secret before it is shown.
- Using every fact in the brief. Select; leave things out.
- Length inflation past the ask.
